question.text: What should you do before you back up?

answer.text: Before you back up, walk around the vehicle to be sure nothing is behind it, and look to the front, both sides and the rear.

teaching.text: Before reversing, walk around the vehicle to make sure nothing is behind it, then look to the front, both sides and the rear. Remember: Walk around, look everywhere.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Before you back up, walk around the vehicle to be sure nothing is behind it, and look to the front, both sides and the rear.

question.text: Where should you keep looking while backing up?

answer.text: Keep watching through the rear window the whole time you back up rather than relying only on mirrors or a back-up camera, and back slowly into the closest lane.

teaching.text: Keep looking out the rear window the whole time you reverse instead of relying only on mirrors or a camera, and back slowly. Remember: Eyes out the rear window.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Keep watching through the rear window the whole time you back up rather than relying only on mirrors or a back-up camera, and back slowly into the closest lane.

question.text: How close to the curb must parallel parked wheels be?

answer.text: When parallel parked, the wheels nearest the edge of the road may be no more than twelve inches from the curb.

teaching.text: A parallel parked vehicle's curb-side wheels may sit no more than twelve inches from the curb. Remember: Within a foot of curb.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When parallel parked, the wheels nearest the edge of the road may be no more than twelve inches from the curb.

question.text: How should you leave a parallel parked vehicle?

answer.text: After parallel parking, point the front wheels toward the curb or shoulder, shift into park and set the parking brake, so a vehicle that starts rolling heads for the curb rather than a traffic lane.

teaching.text: After parallel parking, turn the front wheels to the curb, shift into park and set the brake so a rolling car heads for the curb. Remember: Wheels to curb, park, brake.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After parallel parking, point the front wheels toward the curb or shoulder, shift into park and set the parking brake, so a vehicle that starts rolling heads for the curb rather than a traffic lane.

question.text: Which places are always off limits for parking?

answer.text: Parking is forbidden inside an intersection and on a crosswalk or sidewalk.

teaching.text: Never park inside an intersection, on a crosswalk or on a sidewalk. Remember: Not in intersections or crosswalks.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Parking is forbidden inside an intersection and on a crosswalk or sidewalk.

question.text: How close to a crosswalk at an intersection may you park?

answer.text: You may not park within twenty feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.

teaching.text: Stay at least twenty feet back from a crosswalk at an intersection when you park. Remember: Twenty from the crosswalk.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You may not park within twenty feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.

question.text: How close to a roadside flashing light, stop sign or signal may you park?

answer.text: You may not park within thirty feet of a flashing light, stop sign or traffic control signal standing beside a public road.

teaching.text: Park at least thirty feet from any roadside flashing light, stop sign or traffic control signal. Remember: Thirty from signs and signals.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You may not park within thirty feet of a flashing light, stop sign or traffic control signal standing beside a public road.

question.text: How close to the nearest rail of a railroad crossing may you park?

answer.text: You may not park within fifty feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

teaching.text: Park at least fifty feet from the nearest rail of a railroad crossing. Remember: Fifty from the rail.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You may not park within fifty feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

question.text: How close to a fire hydrant may you park?

answer.text: You may not park within ten feet of a fire hydrant.

teaching.text: Leave at least ten feet between your vehicle and a fire hydrant. Remember: Ten from the hydrant.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You may not park within ten feet of a fire hydrant.

question.text: What are the four no-parking distances?

answer.text: The four no-parking distances on one list are ten feet from a fire hydrant, twenty feet from a crosswalk at an intersection, thirty feet from a roadside flashing light, stop sign or signal, and fifty feet from the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

teaching.text: The four distances climb in order: ten from a hydrant, twenty from a crosswalk, thirty from signals and stop signs, fifty from a rail. Remember: Ten, twenty, thirty, fifty.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The four no-parking distances on one list are ten feet from a fire hydrant, twenty feet from a crosswalk at an intersection, thirty feet from a roadside flashing light, stop sign or signal, and fifty feet from the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

question.text: Which other places ban parking?

answer.text: Parking is also banned on any bridge, inside a highway tunnel and across the street end of a driveway.

teaching.text: Bridges, highway tunnels and the street end of a driveway are also places where you may not park. Remember: Bridges, tunnels, driveway ends.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Parking is also banned on any bridge, inside a highway tunnel and across the street end of a driveway.

question.text: What is double parking, and is it allowed?

answer.text: Stopping on the traffic side of a vehicle already parked at a curb or highway edge is called double parking and is not allowed.

teaching.text: Stopping beside a car already parked at the curb, on its traffic side, is double parking and is not allowed. Remember: Never park beside parked cars.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Stopping on the traffic side of a vehicle already parked at a curb or highway edge is called double parking and is not allowed.

question.text: Which marked or blocked spots also ban parking?

answer.text: You also may not park beside a yellow-painted curb, where official No Parking signs stand, next to or opposite an excavation or obstacle if you would block traffic, or in front of mailboxes where local rules forbid it.

teaching.text: Yellow-painted curbs, No Parking signs, spots that block traffic near an excavation, and restricted mailbox areas are off limits too. Remember: Yellow curbs, signs, digs, mailboxes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You also may not park beside a yellow-painted curb, where official No Parking signs stand, next to or opposite an excavation or obstacle if you would block traffic, or in front of mailboxes where local rules forbid it.

question.text: What should you do before opening a door at the roadside?

answer.text: When stopped or parked at the roadside, check for approaching vehicles, motorcycles, bicyclists and pedestrians before opening any door, and keep a traffic-side door open only as long as loading or unloading needs.

teaching.text: Before opening a door at the roadside, check for cars, motorcycles, bicyclists and pedestrians, and close a traffic-side door quickly. Remember: Look before the door opens.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When stopped or parked at the roadside, check for approaching vehicles, motorcycles, bicyclists and pedestrians before opening any door, and keep a traffic-side door open only as long as loading or unloading needs.

question.text: Which way do you turn the wheels when parking facing downhill?

answer.text: When a parked vehicle faces downhill, turn the wheels toward the curb or the road's shoulder.

teaching.text: Facing downhill, turn the front wheels toward the curb or the shoulder. Remember: Downhill: wheels to the curb.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When a parked vehicle faces downhill, turn the wheels toward the curb or the road's shoulder.

question.text: Which way do you turn the wheels when parking facing uphill next to a curb?

answer.text: When a parked vehicle faces uphill next to a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb.

teaching.text: Facing uphill beside a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb. Remember: Uphill with curb: turn away.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When a parked vehicle faces uphill next to a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb.

question.text: Which way do you turn the wheels when parking facing uphill with no curb?

answer.text: When a parked vehicle faces uphill where there is no curb, turn the wheels toward the shoulder.

teaching.text: Facing uphill with no curb, turn the front wheels toward the shoulder. Remember: No curb: toward the shoulder.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When a parked vehicle faces uphill where there is no curb, turn the wheels toward the shoulder.

question.text: In which single hill parking case do the wheels turn away from the edge?

answer.text: Downhill with or without a curb and uphill without a curb, the wheels turn toward the edge of the road; only uphill with a curb do they turn away from it.

teaching.text: Every hill case turns the wheels toward the edge except uphill with a curb, which turns them away. Remember: Only uphill curb turns away.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Downhill with or without a curb and uphill without a curb, the wheels turn toward the edge of the road; only uphill with a curb do they turn away from it.

question.text: Where do you stop to begin parallel parking?

answer.text: To start parallel parking, stop beside the car ahead of the space, level with it and roughly one and a half feet away.

teaching.text: Begin parallel parking level with the car in front of the space, about one and a half feet from its side. Remember: Even with the car ahead.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To start parallel parking, stop beside the car ahead of the space, level with it and roughly one and a half feet away.

question.text: What are the steering steps for parallel parking?

answer.text: In the parallel parking steps you turn the wheel sharply right and back slowly, turn sharply left once clear of the car ahead while still backing, then turn sharply right and pull toward the curb in the middle of the space.

teaching.text: Steer sharply right while backing, sharply left once clear of the car ahead, then sharply right to settle in the middle of the space. Remember: Right, left, right again.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In the parallel parking steps you turn the wheel sharply right and back slowly, turn sharply left once clear of the car ahead while still backing, then turn sharply right and pull toward the curb in the middle of the space.

question.text: What lights must a vehicle parked on a highway show at night?

answer.text: A vehicle parked on a highway at night, or whenever lights are needed, must show at least one white or amber front light and one red taillight, each visible from at least five hundred feet.

teaching.text: At night, a vehicle parked on a highway must show a white or amber front light and a red taillight, each visible from five hundred feet. Remember: Front light, red tail, visible.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A vehicle parked on a highway at night, or whenever lights are needed, must show at least one white or amber front light and one red taillight, each visible from at least five hundred feet.

question.text: What should you do with a vehicle parked on a state highway or freeway?

answer.text: On a state highway or freeway, move a parked vehicle off the main part of the road, and if it cannot be moved, put out visible markers or signals so other drivers are not harmed.

teaching.text: Move a parked vehicle off the main roadway of a state highway or freeway, or mark it clearly if it cannot be moved. Remember: Off the road or marked.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a state highway or freeway, move a parked vehicle off the main part of the road, and if it cannot be moved, put out visible markers or signals so other drivers are not harmed.

question.text: Which lights should a vehicle parked on the highway use?

answer.text: A vehicle parked on the highway should use parking lights or hazard warning lights to alert others, with any headlights set to low beam.

teaching.text: A vehicle parked on the highway should show parking or hazard lights, with headlights dimmed to low beam. Remember: Hazards on, headlights low.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A vehicle parked on the highway should use parking lights or hazard warning lights to alert others, with any headlights set to low beam.

question.text: Who is responsible for every passenger's safety?

answer.text: As the driver you are responsible for every passenger's safety, so insist that everyone buckles up and that children ride in a restraint suited to their age.

teaching.text: The driver answers for every passenger's safety, so insist on belts for all and the right restraint for each child. Remember: Driver owns passenger safety.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: As the driver you are responsible for every passenger's safety, so insist that everyone buckles up and that children ride in a restraint suited to their age.

question.text: Who must wear seat belts, and can you be stopped for a belt violation alone?

answer.text: Every person in the vehicle, front and back, must wear a properly adjusted and fastened seat belt, and an officer may stop a driver for a seat belt violation alone.

teaching.text: Everyone in the vehicle, front and back, must wear a properly fastened belt, and an officer can stop you for that alone. Remember: Everyone buckles; officers can stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Every person in the vehicle, front and back, must wear a properly adjusted and fastened seat belt, and an officer may stop a driver for a seat belt violation alone.

question.text: Why is the seat belt called the most important safety equipment?

answer.text: The seat belt is called the most important safety equipment in the vehicle, and it keeps occupants from being thrown out, which usually brings death or serious injury.

teaching.text: The seat belt is the most important safety equipment you have, because it keeps you from being thrown out in a crash. Remember: Belts keep you inside.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The seat belt is called the most important safety equipment in the vehicle, and it keeps occupants from being thrown out, which usually brings death or serious injury.

question.text: How much more likely are unbelted riders to be killed or injured?

answer.text: Riding without a seat belt makes you four times more likely to be killed or injured in a crash.

teaching.text: Riding without a belt makes you four times more likely to be killed or injured in a crash. Remember: Unbelted, four times the risk.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Riding without a seat belt makes you four times more likely to be killed or injured in a crash.

question.text: Can an unbelted occupant die in a low-speed crash?

answer.text: An unbelted occupant can die in a crash at speeds as low as twelve miles per hour

teaching.text: An unbelted person can die in a crash even at twelve miles per hour. Remember: Low speed can still kill.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An unbelted occupant can die in a crash at speeds as low as twelve miles per hour

question.text: Which three cases are exempt from the belt law?

answer.text: The belt law does not apply to someone driving a passenger vehicle in reverse, to a rider whose seat belts are all taken by other passengers, or to a person holding a doctor's written certificate for medical reasons.

teaching.text: Only three common cases skip the belt law: reversing a passenger vehicle, every belt already in use, or a doctor's written certificate. Remember: Reverse, full seats, doctor's note.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The belt law does not apply to someone driving a passenger vehicle in reverse, to a rider whose seat belts are all taken by other passengers, or to a person holding a doctor's written certificate for medical reasons.

question.text: When are workers who get in and out often exempt from wearing belts?

answer.text: Workers whose job means getting in and out of the vehicle often are exempt from wearing a belt only while they drive no faster than twenty-five miles per hour

teaching.text: Workers who constantly get in and out are exempt only while driving at twenty-five miles per hour or slower. Remember: Frequent stops, slow speeds only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Workers whose job means getting in and out of the vehicle often are exempt from wearing a belt only while they drive no faster than twenty-five miles per hour

question.text: Which other drivers and vehicles are exempt from the belt law?

answer.text: Other belt exemptions cover a rural mail carrier delivering for the U.S. Postal Service, a person driving or riding in a pickup during farm work, and a vehicle built before Jan. one, one thousand nine hundred sixty-five.

teaching.text: Rural mail carriers on their route, people in a pickup doing farm work and vehicles built before the nineteen sixty-five cutoff are also exempt. Remember: Mail, farm pickup, old car.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Other belt exemptions cover a rural mail carrier delivering for the U.S. Postal Service, a person driving or riding in a pickup during farm work, and a vehicle built before Jan. one, one thousand nine hundred sixty-five.

question.text: How narrow are the speed and reverse belt exemptions?

answer.text: Belt exemptions are narrow: a worker who gets in and out often loses the exemption above twenty-five miles per hour, while a driver of a passenger vehicle is exempt only while backing up.

teaching.text: The exemptions are narrow: the worker exemption ends above twenty-five, and the reverse exemption lasts only while backing. Remember: Exemptions end quickly.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Belt exemptions are narrow: a worker who gets in and out often loses the exemption above twenty-five miles per hour, while a driver of a passenger vehicle is exempt only while backing up.

question.text: How should the lap and shoulder belts fit?

answer.text: Wear the lap belt snug across the hipbones or upper thighs and never across the soft part of the stomach, and the shoulder belt snug across the chest and the middle of the shoulder, using both together.

teaching.text: Wear the lap belt low across the hips or upper thighs, never the soft stomach, and the shoulder belt across the chest and mid-shoulder. Remember: Hips low, chest across.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Wear the lap belt snug across the hipbones or upper thighs and never across the soft part of the stomach, and the shoulder belt snug across the chest and the middle of the shoulder, using both together.

question.text: Where must children under thirteen ride?

answer.text: Children younger than thirteen must ride in the back seat whenever a back seat is available.

teaching.text: Children under thirteen ride in the back seat whenever there is one. Remember: Under thirteen ride in back.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Children younger than thirteen must ride in the back seat whenever a back seat is available.

question.text: What rules apply to car seats and booster seats?

answer.text: Car seats and booster seats must be federally approved and installed the way the manufacturer instructs.

teaching.text: Every car seat and booster must be federally approved and installed exactly as the manufacturer directs. Remember: Approved seats, installed right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Car seats and booster seats must be federally approved and installed the way the manufacturer instructs.

question.text: How long does a child under two ride rear-facing?

answer.text: A child under two rides rear-facing until reaching the seat's height or weight limit, and a child who turns two while still within those limits keeps riding rear-facing.

teaching.text: Babies under two ride rear-facing until they reach the seat's limit, and they stay rear-facing after turning two if still within it. Remember: Rear-facing to the limit.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A child under two rides rear-facing until reaching the seat's height or weight limit, and a child who turns two while still within those limits keeps riding rear-facing.

question.text: When does a child ride in a forward-facing car seat?

answer.text: A child older than two who has outgrown the rear-facing limits rides in a forward-facing car seat until reaching its limit, which is usually forty to sixty pounds depending on the maker.

teaching.text: Once a child over two outgrows rear-facing, a forward-facing seat comes next, usually up to forty to sixty pounds. Remember: Outgrew rear, now forward.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A child older than two who has outgrown the rear-facing limits rides in a forward-facing car seat until reaching its limit, which is usually forty to sixty pounds depending on the maker.

question.text: Who must use a booster seat with a safety belt?

answer.text: A child aged four to nine who has outgrown the car seat must use a booster seat together with a safety belt.

teaching.text: Children from four to nine who have outgrown the car seat ride in a booster with a safety belt. Remember: Four to nine, boost them.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A child aged four to nine who has outgrown the car seat must use a booster seat together with a safety belt.

question.text: When does a child move from the booster to the seat belt alone?

answer.text: At age nine, or once a child exceeds the booster seat's height or weight limit, the child rides without the booster but buckled in a seat belt.

teaching.text: At nine, or once too big for the booster, a child rides buckled in a seat belt without the booster. Remember: Nine or too big: belt.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At age nine, or once a child exceeds the booster seat's height or weight limit, the child rides without the booster but buckled in a seat belt.

question.text: Which age ranges do the rear-facing and booster stages cover?

answer.text: Rear-facing is the rule for a child under two until the seat's limit is reached, while the booster stage covers children aged four to nine who have outgrown their car seat.

teaching.text: Rear-facing covers children under two until the seat limit, and the booster stage covers ages four to nine. Remember: Rear under two, boost four-nine.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Rear-facing is the rule for a child under two until the seat's limit is reached, while the booster stage covers children aged four to nine who have outgrown their car seat.

question.text: When does a child restraint expire, and what about seats in crashes?

answer.text: Child restraints expire six years after they are made unless a different date is stamped on the seat, and a seat that has been in a crash should not be used again.

teaching.text: Child seats expire six years after manufacture unless stamped otherwise, and a seat that has been in a crash should be replaced. Remember: Six years, never after crash.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Child restraints expire six years after they are made unless a different date is stamped on the seat, and a seat that has been in a crash should not be used again.

question.text: How do you tell when a child seat with no stamped date expires?

answer.text: If a child seat has no expiration date stamped on it, follow the six-year rule counted from the date it was made.

teaching.text: With no stamped date, count six years from the date the seat was made, not the date you bought it. Remember: No date, count six years.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If a child seat has no expiration date stamped on it, follow the six-year rule counted from the date it was made.

question.text: Where must a rear-facing infant seat never go?

answer.text: Never put a rear-facing infant seat in front of an active airbag, never carry a child on a passenger's lap, and do not let children ride in the cargo area of a truck or station wagon.

teaching.text: Never place a rear-facing seat in front of an active airbag, never hold a child on a lap, and keep children out of cargo areas. Remember: Never facing an airbag.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never put a rear-facing infant seat in front of an active airbag, never carry a child on a passenger's lap, and do not let children ride in the cargo area of a truck or station wagon.

question.text: Why should children never be left alone in a vehicle?

answer.text: Never leave children or vulnerable adults alone in a vehicle, because they could set it in motion, face deadly heat or cold, be in a car that is stolen, or be harmed by someone breaking in.

teaching.text: Never leave children or vulnerable adults alone in a vehicle; they could move it, suffer heat or cold, or be harmed in a theft. Remember: Never leave kids alone.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never leave children or vulnerable adults alone in a vehicle, because they could set it in motion, face deadly heat or cold, be in a car that is stolen, or be harmed by someone breaking in.

question.text: How should you protect your vehicle against theft?

answer.text: To guard against theft, lock the doors, take the keys with you, never leave the engine running, and leave nothing that looks valuable in sight.

teaching.text: Lock the doors, take your keys, never leave the engine running and keep anything that looks valuable out of sight. Remember: Lock, keys out, hide valuables.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To guard against theft, lock the doors, take the keys with you, never leave the engine running, and leave nothing that looks valuable in sight.

question.text: Why should pets not be left in a vehicle?

answer.text: Pets should not be left in a vehicle, especially on very hot or very cold days, because extreme temperatures can be very dangerous for animals.

teaching.text: Do not leave pets in a vehicle, especially on very hot or cold days, because extreme temperatures endanger animals. Remember: Heat and cold endanger pets.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Pets should not be left in a vehicle, especially on very hot or very cold days, because extreme temperatures can be very dangerous for animals.

question.text: What can and cannot an airbag do?

answer.text: An airbag is a supplemental restraint system that helps a seat belt prevent injuries but is not built to stop you from being thrown out.

teaching.text: An airbag adds protection alongside the seat belt, but it cannot keep you from being thrown out. Remember: Airbags assist, belts restrain.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An airbag is a supplemental restraint system that helps a seat belt prevent injuries but is not built to stop you from being thrown out.

question.text: What back seat rule does the airbag page repeat?

answer.text: The airbag page repeats, for safety reasons, that children under age thirteen must ride in the back seat whenever one is available.

teaching.text: The airbag section repeats that children under thirteen should ride in the back seat when one is available. Remember: Under thirteen still in back.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The airbag page repeats, for safety reasons, that children under age thirteen must ride in the back seat whenever one is available.

question.text: How far should you sit from the steering wheel?

answer.text: Keep at least ten inches between your body and the steering wheel.

teaching.text: Sit so there are at least ten inches between your body and the steering wheel. Remember: Ten inches from the wheel.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Keep at least ten inches between your body and the steering wheel.

question.text: Where should you hold the steering wheel?

answer.text: Hold the wheel at the eight and four or the nine and three o'clock positions with thumbs turned outward, and avoid the ten and two o'clock position.

teaching.text: Grip the wheel at eight and four or nine and three with thumbs pointing out, and avoid ten and two. Remember: Eight-four or nine-three.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Hold the wheel at the eight and four or the nine and three o'clock positions with thumbs turned outward, and avoid the ten and two o'clock position.

question.text: What should front passengers do in a vehicle with airbags?

answer.text: Move front passenger seats as far back as they go, and read the operator's manual before driving or riding in a vehicle with airbags.

teaching.text: Slide front passenger seats as far back as they go, and read the operator's manual about your airbags. Remember: Front seat back, read manual.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Move front passenger seats as far back as they go, and read the operator's manual before driving or riding in a vehicle with airbags.

question.text: What may you throw from a vehicle onto roads or land?

answer.text: Throwing or dumping anything from a vehicle onto roads or public or private land is illegal, including cigarettes, fireworks, snow, ice, glass, nails, cans, garbage, ashes and animal carcasses.

teaching.text: Throwing anything from a vehicle onto roads or land is illegal, from cigarettes and fireworks to snow, ice and garbage. Remember: Nothing goes out the window.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Throwing or dumping anything from a vehicle onto roads or public or private land is illegal, including cigarettes, fireworks, snow, ice, glass, nails, cans, garbage, ashes and animal carcasses.

question.text: What are your first steps after a crash?

answer.text: After a crash, stop, move out of the driving lane onto the shoulder if you can, and switch off the ignition to lower the fire risk.

teaching.text: After a crash, stop, get onto the shoulder if you can and turn off the ignition to reduce fire risk. Remember: Stop, shoulder, ignition off.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After a crash, stop, move out of the driving lane onto the shoulder if you can, and switch off the ignition to lower the fire risk.

question.text: How do you warn approaching drivers of a crash scene?

answer.text: Warn approaching drivers of a crash scene with emergency flashers, flares or a flashlight.

teaching.text: Warn drivers approaching a crash with emergency flashers, flares or a flashlight. Remember: Flashers, flares, flashlight.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Warn approaching drivers of a crash scene with emergency flashers, flares or a flashlight.

question.text: When must you call law enforcement or emergency services after a crash?

answer.text: If anyone is hurt or killed in the crash, call the nearest law enforcement agency or nine hundred eleven as fast as you can.

teaching.text: If anyone is hurt or killed, call the nearest law enforcement agency or nine one one right away. Remember: Hurt or killed: call.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If anyone is hurt or killed in the crash, call the nearest law enforcement agency or nine hundred eleven as fast as you can.

question.text: What help does the law require you to give crash victims?

answer.text: The law requires you to give crash victims reasonable assistance, giving first aid if you are able and qualified, or otherwise keeping the injured comfortable.

teaching.text: You must give crash victims reasonable help, first aid if you are able and qualified, or at least keep them comfortable. Remember: Reasonable help, first aid.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The law requires you to give crash victims reasonable assistance, giving first aid if you are able and qualified, or otherwise keeping the injured comfortable.

question.text: What information do you give the other drivers and officers?

answer.text: Give the other drivers and any officer at the scene your name, address, date of birth and vehicle registration number, and show your driver's license to anyone who asks.

teaching.text: Give the other drivers and officers your name, address, date of birth and registration number, and show your license when asked. Remember: Name, address, birthday, registration.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Give the other drivers and any officer at the scene your name, address, date of birth and vehicle registration number, and show your driver's license to anyone who asks.

question.text: What if you do not have your insurance details at the scene?

answer.text: If asked, give your insurer's name and address and your agent's name, and if you do not have them with you, provide them within seventy-two hours.

teaching.text: If you are asked for insurance details and lack them, provide your insurer's name and address and agent's name within seventy-two hours. Remember: Insurance info within seventy-two.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If asked, give your insurer's name and address and your agent's name, and if you do not have them with you, provide them within seventy-two hours.

question.text: What must you do after a crash that damages only property?

answer.text: A crash that damages only property does not have to be reported to law enforcement, but tow a disabled vehicle quickly and tell the owner of any other property you damaged.

teaching.text: A crash with only property damage needs no police report, but tow a disabled vehicle and tell the owner of anything else you damaged. Remember: Tow it, tell owners.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A crash that damages only property does not have to be reported to law enforcement, but tow a disabled vehicle quickly and tell the owner of any other property you damaged.

question.text: How do injury crashes and property-only crashes differ for reporting?

answer.text: A crash that hurts or kills someone requires a call to law enforcement or nine hundred eleven, while a property-damage-only crash needs no police notice, only towing if disabled and telling any other property owner.

teaching.text: Injuries or deaths mean calling for help; property-only damage means towing if needed and telling other owners. Remember: Injury calls; property doesn't.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A crash that hurts or kills someone requires a call to law enforcement or nine hundred eleven, while a property-damage-only crash needs no police notice, only towing if disabled and telling any other property owner.

question.text: What insurance must the owner of a vehicle driven on public roads carry?

answer.text: An owner whose vehicle is driven on public roads must carry no-fault and liability insurance and keep valid proof of it in the vehicle at all times.

teaching.text: Every vehicle used on public roads needs no-fault and liability insurance, with proof kept inside the vehicle. Remember: No-fault plus liability, proof.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An owner whose vehicle is driven on public roads must carry no-fault and liability insurance and keep valid proof of it in the vehicle at all times.

question.text: What can happen if you cannot show proof of insurance?

answer.text: Not producing proof of insurance when an officer asks can lead to revocation of your driver's license and your vehicle registration.

teaching.text: Failing to show proof of insurance to an officer can lead to losing your license and your vehicle registration. Remember: No proof, lose license.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Not producing proof of insurance when an officer asks can lead to revocation of your driver's license and your vehicle registration.

question.text: What must you do to get privileges back after an insurance revocation?

answer.text: To get driving privileges back after an insurance revocation, you take and pass a written test, pay a thirty dollars reinstatement fee on top of any court fines or citations, apply for a new license and file an insurance certificate from your insurer.

teaching.text: After an insurance revocation, pass a written test, pay the thirty-dollar fee and any fines, apply for a license and file an insurance certificate. Remember: Test, fee, apply, certificate.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To get driving privileges back after an insurance revocation, you take and pass a written test, pay a thirty dollars reinstatement fee on top of any court fines or citations, apply for a new license and file an insurance certificate from your insurer.

question.text: What penalties can a conviction for driving uninsured bring?

answer.text: A conviction for driving an uninsured vehicle can bring a fine of up to one thousand dollars and up to ninety days in jail, and driving privileges may be revoked for up to one year.

teaching.text: Driving uninsured can bring up to a thousand-dollar fine, up to ninety days in jail and up to a year's revocation. Remember: Uninsured: fine, jail, revocation.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A conviction for driving an uninsured vehicle can bring a fine of up to one thousand dollars and up to ninety days in jail, and driving privileges may be revoked for up to one year.

question.text: What insurance must motorcycle drivers carry?

answer.text: Motorcycle drivers must carry liability coverage for property damage and injuries to others, while no-fault and uninsured driver coverage is optional for them.

teaching.text: Motorcyclists must carry liability coverage, while no-fault and uninsured driver coverage are optional for them. Remember: Riders need liability coverage.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Motorcycle drivers must carry liability coverage for property damage and injuries to others, while no-fault and uninsured driver coverage is optional for them.

question.text: What else can running an uninsured vehicle cost?

answer.text: Running an uninsured vehicle can also cost the vehicle's license plates and registration, separate from any court penalty.

teaching.text: An uninsured vehicle can also lose its license plates and registration, apart from any court penalty. Remember: Plates and registration too.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Running an uninsured vehicle can also cost the vehicle's license plates and registration, separate from any court penalty.

question.text: How do the insurance reinstatement fee and the messaging and uninsured fines compare?

answer.text: The insurance reinstatement fee is thirty, dollars while the repeat messaging fine is two hundred seventy-five dollars and the uninsured-vehicle fine can reach one thousand dollars.

teaching.text: Thirty dollars is the reinstatement fee, two hundred seventy-five is the repeat texting fine, and up to one thousand is the uninsured fine. Remember: Fee small, fines bigger.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The insurance reinstatement fee is thirty, dollars while the repeat messaging fine is two hundred seventy-five dollars and the uninsured-vehicle fine can reach one thousand dollars.

question.text: How long does a new resident have to register a vehicle?

answer.text: A new Minnesota resident has up to sixty days to register each vehicle driven on public roads with DVS.

teaching.text: New residents have up to sixty days to register each vehicle they drive on public roads. Remember: Register within sixty days.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A new Minnesota resident has up to sixty days to register each vehicle driven on public roads with DVS.

question.text: What do you bring to register a vehicle?

answer.text: To register a vehicle, take its current title or registration card and your driver's license or other valid ID to the nearest deputy registrar's office.

teaching.text: Bring the title or registration card plus your license or ID to the nearest deputy registrar to register a vehicle. Remember: Title plus ID to registrar.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To register a vehicle, take its current title or registration card and your driver's license or other valid ID to the nearest deputy registrar's office.

question.text: What phone uses are banned while driving?

answer.text: While driving you may not use a phone or other wireless device to write, read or send emails, texts or instant messages, or to go online.

teaching.text: While driving, never write, read or send texts, emails or instant messages, and never go online. Remember: No texts, email or browsing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: While driving you may not use a phone or other wireless device to write, read or send emails, texts or instant messages, or to go online.

question.text: Which phone uses does the messaging ban not cover?

answer.text: The messaging ban does not cover calling for emergency help, reporting a crash or crime, or using the device in voice-activated or hands-free mode.

teaching.text: Calling for emergency help, reporting a crash or crime, and voice-activated or hands-free use are outside the messaging ban. Remember: Emergencies and hands-free allowed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The messaging ban does not cover calling for emergency help, reporting a crash or crime, or using the device in voice-activated or hands-free mode.

question.text: What extra fine applies after two or more messaging convictions?

answer.text: A driver convicted two or more times of messaging while driving must pay a two hundred seventy-five dollars fine on top of the fine the court sets.

teaching.text: A second or later messaging conviction adds a two hundred seventy-five dollar fine to the court's fine. Remember: Repeat texters pay extra.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A driver convicted two or more times of messaging while driving must pay a two hundred seventy-five dollars fine on top of the fine the court sets.
